This is an entertaining dissertation from 2008 in which George Knapp relates a myriad of strange events about the notorious Skinwalker Ranch in NE Utah as told to him by the various residents of the ranch and local townspeople. The difficult to categorize phenomena is said to continue to this day.

Of particular interest is the involvement of Robert Bigelow, the Ranch's current owner. Bigelow is a Las Vegas motel tycoon who used his fortune to stake his private space company, Bigelow Aeronautics. Notably, Bigelow Aeronautics recently contracted with SpaceX to ferry inflatable modular space station compartments into orbit.

Robert Bigelow purchased the storied property and populated it with a science and security team to investigate the unusual and often frightening happenings. Skinwalker Ranch is situated on 480 acres of forbidden Ute Indian ground, in the middle of a reservation surrounding it on all sides with a single road leading in. Elements of cryptozoology, poltergeist, animal mutilation, and UFO behavior, among others, combine to lead many to believe that Skinwalker Ranch is inhabited by one or more highly intelligent Trickster like beings, capricious in nature and apparently capable of manifesting both physical and illusory form. Whatever occupies the property possesses inhuman intelligence, and has allegedly been witnessed coming and going from portals, tunnels, and voids to some other plane or place. This particular behavior is attributed both to the animal as well as the UFO manifestations of the phenomena. Robert Bigelow believes the entity to be dangerous, and others have described it as evil.

Linux is open-source, meaning every bit of code that is run when you use Linux can be viewed online. If tracking code was added to the kernel it would be spotted and reported. The same goes for almost all software that is used in distros. They are open-source meaning that when compiled you can see what the resulting binary should look like, and using checksums confirm that it is the same as the binary that was packaged with the distro. It also means that any tracking code that is added to the software will be spotted by someone and reported.

If I extrapolate the meaning of "should look like" this statement can be true-ish, but this sounds like an odd misconception. Sorry to seem pedantic, but this topic is too often over-laymenized. Open source only means the source is accessible and not proprietary.

Most of linux (with the exception of Ubuntu with Unity) doesn't actually provide much trackable information from the OS. It's usually leaked/shared by apps.

With apps, the usual warnings about firefox and google chrome still hold.

im not sure about big and proprietary apps, but technically, if you got access to the source code, and you're understand about programming, you can read the source code itself, and find whether it contains malicious code or not

Fact 1: Opensource means that you, and everyone else, can peek under the hood.

Fact 2: The community that uses linux tends to be very privacy-centric.

From these two facts, we can deduce that if a linux distro were tracking you (Cough Ubuntu Cough), then someone on the internet will find out and raise the alarm.

Linux and open source software is not supposed to track you. While it is technically possible someone could sneak in malicious tracking code, there are many developers out there who watch out for this type of stuff. So while it is possible a piece of open source software could track it, it is much less likely that say Windows, which we already know tracks you.

Also, some distros have tracking of some kind or another, either as opt-in or opt-out. For example, Ubuntu had opt-out tracking by Amazon for a long time. I am not sure if they still do. Debian has an opt-in tracking package called "popularity contest", which is used to evaluate the popularity of various software packages. The key difference in this case is that Ubuntu's tracking was enabled by default, and was used to make Canonical money, while Debian's is disabled by default, and is used to aid the development of the Debian project. Tracking of both varieties is not unheard of in many distros, although the latter (non-malicious) variety is more common, and most respectable distros leave it disable by default.

18If the world hate you, ye know that it hated me before it hated you. 19If ye were of the world, the world would love his own: but because ye are not of the world, but I have chosen you out of the world, therefore the world hateth you. - John 15:18-19 (KJV)

 It is a truth that if you serve the Lord with all your heart, and let your light shine out into this dark world, the world will hate you. Jesus suffered this hate and cruelty from the world, as they rejected and crucified Him. By coming and suffering, as we suffer, Jesus became the perfect High Priest for us, as He was tempted in all the ways that we are (Hebrews 4:15-16). Just think about the fact that Jesus was the creator of man (Ephesians 3:9), and yet He took on the form of a man and came to earth, just to redeem us, and bring us back into fellowship with the Father (John 17:3). No matter how much we are persecuted for Jesus, it can not compare to what Jesus went through for us.

 You can be sure that if you live a Christian life, the world will hate you, as it hated Jesus (2 Timothy 3:12). It is not really you it hates, but it is Jesus living through you that upsets this world, as the light you shine forth (holiness), exposes the darkness (sin) in the world. If you are born again, you truly are not of this world (1 Peter 2:9), as you are a part of the body of Christ, who is in heaven, so your home now is in heaven (Hebrews 11:16) – Praise God. What an honor it is to have been chosen by the Lord to be part of His body, and no matter what persecution befalls us, we should rejoice, as our rewards in heaven will more then compensate us (Matthew 5:11-12). Praise God for all His promises in the bible.

Devotional by Pastor Joe W. Green, www.Infinite-Faith.com
